text:
Liam: Quick heads-up — I'm kicking off a targeted load synthesis to set sane defaults for RPM/TPM and burst handling across text-gen routes. Goal: find thresholds that keep 95p latency < 350ms and error rate < 0.5%. Running now, will post results.

Maya: Nice — what's the plan for bursts vs steady-state?

Liam: Plan: 10m steady phases at 200/600/1200 RPM, then 3x and 5x 60s spike bursts on top of each steady. Also run token-heavy runs to exercise TPM limits. Using our loadlab harness (k6 + request multiplex) so patterns match real clients.

Jon: Can you drop the command you're using so I can reproduce locally?

Liam: sure — example:```bash
loadlab run --scenario text-gen-steady --rpm 1200 --duration 600 --burst-spike 3x --burst-length 60 --token-weight 1.2
```

Priya: FYI support has a customer complaining about 429s last night, might be useful to replay their pattern (short bursts of many small requests). I can attach sample traffic dump.

support-oncall: attaching a sanitized trace now — mostly 40-60 reqs/sec sustained for 3m then a short 30s spike. We saw client-side retry loops which amplified RPM.

Maya: Good call. We'll include a "chatty client" pattern that does 10rps per connection with retries (exponential backoff disabled) so we capture retry amplification.

loadlab-bot: started run id=622 (text-gen-steady, rpm=1200, burst=3x). Logs will appear in /runs/622/

Liam: Initial 1200RPM steady run: 95p ~ 310ms, p99 ~ 480ms (cold starts in first minute), error 0.3%. Spike (3x) produced brief 429 surge to 2.8% and latency p95 jumped to 720ms for ~20s.

Jon: Did KV cache warm-ups or model load happen on those spikes?

Maya: Checked traces — KV cache warmed gradually; model stayed resident. The latency spike correlates with request queueing on the router before batching. Our kernel selection handles bursts poorly if request queue depth exceeds batch window.

Priya: Any quick mitigations we can push to prod for customers seeing 429s?

Liam: Short-term: increase per-route burst token bucket size for affected customers by 2x for 10m, and apply small configurable retry jitter on client SDKs. Medium-term: adjust burst_window to 60s with a larger capacity token-bucket and prioritize tiny requests into separate fast-path pool.

Maya: From runs, recommended safe defaults: global per-key RPM = 600, TPM = 18,000, burst multiplier = 3x over a 60s window. Token bucket size = burst_multiplier * (RPM / 60) * 60 => simplify to burst_multiplier * RPM (so default bucket = 1800 tokens for RPM=600).

Jon: I like default RPM 600 — gives 10 RPS steady. For enterprise/dedicated tiers we can raise to 2k RPM with tighter monitoring.

support-oncall: For customer support playbook: if customer reports latency/429s, ask for request timestamps + client retry behavior, check per-key RPM/TMP usage, and suggest temporary per-key burst uplift while we run targeted replay.

Priya: One more observation — token-heavy runs (high TPM) caused similar 429s earlier than pure RPM runs. That suggests our enforcement counts token units before we consider batching efficiency. Might need to decouple token enforcement from short-request fast-path.

Liam: Agreed. Action items: 1) update loadlab scenarios with chatty-client pattern (Jon) 2) add burst-window 60s + bucket calc to policy docs (Maya) 3) patch console to show token-bucket state and recent bursts for a key (Priya) 4) ops run rolling canary with new burst defaults on staging (Liam). I'll post a summary after the full sweep.

Maya: +1 — and add a checkbox in support playbook to ask for SDK version (old SDKs cause aggressive retries).

Jon: re: scripts — I'll add a small script to convert support trace -> loadlab input. Will push in ~2h.

loadlab-bot: run id=622 finished. artifacts: /runs/622/summary.json /runs/622/plots.zip

Liam: Summary posted to /runs/622/summary.json — TL;DR: steady 1200RPM borderline for 95p; defaults we recommend are more conservative (600RPM) unless customer is on Dedicated or has rate-limited client code. Leaving this thread open for comments. :thumbsup:
